input.quote: Upon creation and subject to payment of the applicable Fees, Customer owns each Deliverable created specifically for Customer. Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all worldwide right, title, and interest in those Deliverables and shall obtain equivalent assignments from its personnel.
input.rationale: The IP package meets our preferred position in full. Section 14.1 confirms Customer owns all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information and pre-existing/independently developed IP, with no transfer to Vendor beyond a limited processing right to deliver the Services; Section 15.1 reinforces this by barring sale, advertising use, data commingling and model training without our written consent. Section 14.2 vests ownership of each Deliverable in Customer on creation with an express present assignment plus personnel assignments and further-assurance cooperation. Section 14.3 lets Vendor retain only Vendor Technology while pulling in the Section 13.2 perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence (including rights to modify, create derivative works and use contractors) for any Vendor Technology embedded in or needed to use a Deliverable, and requires disclosure of embedded Vendor IP and consent before adding restrictive third-party material. Section 14.4 expressly negates joint ownership absent a signed separate instrument and keeps feedback rights with us. Two minor points noted only, not deviations: "Deliverable" (1.4) is limited to work product an Order Form identifies as created specifically for Customer, so Order Forms should be drafted to capture all bespoke work product; and the Deliverable ownership is conditioned on payment of the applicable Fees, which is customary. No redline proposed.
